headline: Approved 30-lot Woodlands Reserve subdivision off Parkside Drive; approved 1-year extension for UNE pier at 11 Hills Beach Road; recommended data center ban.
summary: Approved a 30-lot subdivision off Parkside Drive, a site plan amendment for 46-unit senior housing on Barra Road, and a shoreland permit at 41 Bridge Road. A 3-2 vote approved a 1-year extension for UNE's marine research pier at 11 Hills Beach Road. Recommended City Council adoption of a data center ban, a front yard setback reduction, and new mobile home park setbacks.
decisions: Approved the September 2, 2026 meeting minutes as presented; passed unanimously.
Approved a 1-year extension of the 2025 approval for the Marine Research Science Pier at 11 Hills Beach Road, 3-2.
Approved a conditional use permit for a 1-chair barber shop at 351 West Street; passed unanimously.
Approved a site plan amendment for a 46-unit low-income senior housing development on Barra Road; passed unanimously.
Approved a shoreland permit to replace a legally existing non-conforming home at 41 Bridge Road; passed unanimously.
Approved Subdivision Amendment #2 for Longboard View, a seven-lot subdivision at 781 Pool Street; passed unanimously.
Approved the final site and subdivision plan for the 30-lot Woodlands Reserve off Parkside Drive and 268 Pool Street, with a front yard setback reduction from 40 to 25 feet; passed unanimously.
Recommended City Council adoption of a definition of data centers that prohibits data centers within Biddeford; passed unanimously.
Recommended City Council approval of reducing the minimum front yard setback from forty (40) feet to twenty-five (25) feet in several residential zones; passed unanimously.
Recommended City Council adoption of amended setbacks for mobile home parks, with 10 feet from lot boundary lines; passed unanimously.

transcript:
# PLANNING BOARD MEETING MINUTES

October 7, 2026

1. Pledge of Allegiance-Meeting brought to order at 6:00 PM

2. Declaration of Quorum

Planning Board: John McCurry, Matthew Sargent-Dubois, Roch Angers, Leah Schaffer, Chico Potvin & Rob Nicoll (Alternate Member)

Staff: David Galbraith & Harry Center

3. Adjustments to Agenda-none

4. Planner's Business

Galbraith talked about 2026.47 Planner approval of the proposed doors and new ramp for Blossom Retail, LLC at 45 Boulder Way (Tax Map 2, Lot 56) as a minor amendment to the approved development plans, NOT requiring a site plan amendment before the Planning Board.

5. Consent Agenda

5.a. Approval of Meeting Minutes of September 2, 2026

MOTIONS: 6:00 PM

Motion- Schaffer -Motion to approve Meeting Minutes as presented

Second-Angers

Vote: Motion passed unanimously

6. Unfinished Business

6.a 2026.44 Review of a request from the University of New England (UNE) for a 1-year extension of their 2025 approval to construct a Marine Science Research Pier at 11 Hills Beach Road (Tax Map 52, Lot 4) in the Institutional Zone.

- Tabled at last meeting
- Motion-Schaffer-Motion to remove from the table
- Second-Nicoll
- Vote-Unanimous
- Galbraith reminded the Board that this is only for a 1-year extension to the approval.
- Item was in the courts it was also stayed.
- Not a re-hearing of the case
- Staff believe this has more than validity

MOTION:

Motion-Schaffer-Motion to extend approval for Marine Research Science Pier for 1 year

Second-Potvin

No Public Comments

- Angers-talked about emails received regarding the process, he feels the mooring owners are being told they must move, the harbor master should be consulted.
- Patoine (former Board Member) asked for a report which was never given to board.
- He feels there is something there that they have not been told about it
- Angers feels harbormaster should be involved. He does not feel reasons were ever given as to why harbor master was not included.
- Angers must vote on his integrity, this is like a can of sardines, this smells very fishy, he will not be voting in favor.
- Potvin feels like if they vote no they will be no further and they have more important things to deal with. This will have to go through Codes as well.
- Sargent-Dubois will not be able to support this project due to the harbor master issue.
- Nicoll appreciates the feelings of his colleagues he is not voting this evening; we must be careful to vote the way it is intended which is very straight forward of is the request for an extension valid based on all the reasons why they were not allowed to start construction a year ago. We will be opening a door that will make it very difficult for any progress to be made.
- Potvin asked Galbraith & Center-when they go to pull the permit does the Harbor Master have to sign off on the permit?
- Center answered The harbor master has no role with respect to the Code Office. He sited the ordinance portion that mentions the harbor master and went on to say there are 10 criteria that are limited to other agency approvals i.e. indigenous tribes, army corps... When that ordinance was passed the proponent of the ordinance telling the Policy Committee the Harbor Master is merely a facilitator, the Harbor Master guides the applicant through the process. Two former councilors and (Liam was on the Policy Committee at that time too) said then the Harbor Master approves it and the chair of the Harbor Commission at that time said Absolutely Not, the Harbor Master does Not Grant or approve anything he is merely a facilitator. The language is inconsistent, the problem we run into is the government can't impose regulations on private property without clear constitutionally supportable standards setbacks, height.... There is nothing in the ordinance about depth, current, effect on moorings, other aspects eluded to for placement of the pier. Secondly, as a Planning Board, we go to deny the request without the applicant even being there. We have in public record a Harbor Commission Meeting where the Harbor Commission considered the potential pier and UNE hadn't even applied yet and it said the Harbor Master is going to deny the permit. As City Solicitor, that puts Harry in a spot to find a neutral judge to say that's ok, we had a due process body considered a permit before it was even filed, determined to deny an applicant without giving the applicant the opportunity to be heard. That is the position the City was in and that is why he gave his legal opinion regarding the Harbor Master; it was nothing personal but in his legal opinion it was a flawed process. You cannot deny something before someone applies. Is the extension necessary because it's beyond the university's control? The tree cutting permit was denied due to the language in the moratorium. It said "no permits" period so Codes denied it and it held up in the appeal process. Last night the Council said the pier project and DeCary Hall are not subject to the moratorium. Now the delay the elephant in the room is the 250' buffer zone. It's in maps and the Master Plan and then it's not in a different plan, does this cause the delay, is it because the applicant didn't bring this buffer zone forward. Is this something you can consider when considering the extension.
- Galbraith talked about why extensions are generally granted. In this case the reason the staff is in favor of this is because the City held the University up in getting permits. We base the decision on, is this a valid reason for giving an extension? We've also had the same on shoreland zoning whether they moved forward or not. If they come to us before it expires then we bring it in for an extension if it has already expired, we have no choice but to bring them back to Planning Board as a new request.
- McCurry asked about basing their decision on not knowing about the 250' in the beginning and the case was approved whether the 250' or not and we do not approve the extension request because of the 250' now, we are in essence re-considering something that was approved by the prior Planning Board.
- Galbraith said that is correct and that 250' is not a City regulation, (and Harry can correct me if I'm wrong), that 250' was found in one sentence in the Master Plan of 2004 or 2007 and it has not been in the Master Plan since. There is 250' on the latest plan and it said 250' SRCC, that was their regulation, not the City's regulation and we looked at it by the City's regulation. We are looking at whether we have valid reason to approve this extension.
- Schaffer feels this very cut and dry, and there are only 2 who were on the Planning Board. She does not feel that she has any basis to reinterpret what the previous Board voted on. What she is looking at is the extension request and is UNE able to go forward with this request and get their permits based on anything from their own or outside factors. To her it is cut and dry and she will be voting to approve this request.
- Potvin, in an effort to assist with McCurry's question, gave the scenario of if he went for an extension and the ordinance had changed. In this case the ordinance did not change and the 250' buffer is not our ordinance but the Saco River Corridor's.
- McCurry Thanked Potvin and said he agrees with Schaffer he believes tonight is just the extension. If they were going through this from the beginning there would probably be a different result.
- McCurry Called for a VOTE: Motion passed 3-2 (Potvin, Schaffer & McCurry in favor, Angers & Sargent-Dubois opposed)

7.c 2026.45 The Chisholm Family Irrevocable Trust has applied for a Shoreland Permit (Greatest Practical Extent/GPE) for their property located at 41 Bridge Street (Tax Map 63, Lot 50) in the Coastal Residential and Resource Protection Zone. The applicant is seeking to pursue a one-time expansion of footprint up to 30% of the existing footprints. The proposed building footprint contains 1,478 square feet with a 150 square foot deck.

MOTIONS: 6:39 PM

Motion- Sargent-Dubois-Motion to Approve Case # 2026.45 Review a Shoreland Permit request from the Chisholm Family Revocable Trust (Applicant) to replace a legally existing, non-conforming single-family home located at 41 Bridge Road (Tax Map 63, Lot 50) located within the Coastal Residential (CR) Zone, and Resource Protection (RP) and Limited Residential Shoreland Overlay districts, with the below recommended Conditions of Approval (COA).

1. The new building shall not be relocated closer to any of the existing property lines as noted on the approved plan.

2. The Code Enforcement Officer shall review and approve conformance to Section 15 of the Shoreland Zoning Ordinance.

- Sargent-Dubois asked about an HOA, who is responsible for these inspections? There is a HOA one BMP that has already been constructed and this procedure is already in place.
- Schaffer, question for Galbraith, the clearing meets the ordinance. Is anyone going out to check to make sure they did not exceed the limits of clearing? Galbraith, yes, is in the Conditions of Approval and Codes will be inspecting it.

[Note: The attached file contains five pages numbered 1 to 5, not pages 7 to 11 of 11. The transcript below covers all five pages provided.]

**8.a The Planning Board will have the second reading of the Data Center Ordinance. MOTION: 7:03 PM**

Motion- Schaffer-Motion to forward a positive recommendation to the City Council to adopt the proposed Ordinance Amendment to the City's Code of Ordinance, Part III - Land Development Regulations, Article II - Definitions, to include the below definition of "Data Centers":

Data Center / Data Center Artificial Intelligence (AI): A Data Center is a facility used to house computer systems and associated components, such as telecommunications and storage systems. Data centers provide critical infrastructure for the storage and processing of information, and they support the global financial system, cloud services, machine learning, and artificial intelligence (AI). An AI data center is a specialized facility designed to support the unique requirements of AI workloads. Data centers are prohibited within the City of Biddeford.

Second-Sargent-Dubois

NO PUBLIC COMMENTS

Vote-Motion passed unanimously

**8.b Proposed Ordinance Amendments to the City's Code of Ordinance, Part III - Land Development Regulations, Article V- Establishment of Zones, Table B- Dimensional Requirements. MOTION: 8:18 pm**
